(Benefit)

Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about a man who heard a muezzin say: "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and he said: "You lie." Does he become a disbeliever?

He said: "No. He does not become a disbeliever, because it is possible that his intention was to deny the one who spoke regarding what he said (the word 'no' in the root of the statement), so it is as if he said: 'You do not bear this testimony,' like the saying of Allah: ﴿But Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars.﴾"

The commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 63, verses 2–3:

"They take their oaths as a shield, and so they bar [others] from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing." [al-Munafiqun: 2]

Their oath precedes their speech, without anyone having raised an objection to it, because he knows that the hearts of the people of faith are not at ease with him. So he disclaims [suspicion] by his oath, from ill thoughts about him and from uncovering what he harbors. Likewise, the people of doubt lie and swear oaths so that the listener will reckon that they are truthful. They have "taken their oaths as a shield, and so they bar [others] from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing."

Woe to them! They went out into the open desert with the caravan of faith, but when they saw the length of the road and the distance of the journey, they turned back on their heels and returned, and they thought that they would enjoy the good life and the sweetness of sleep in their homes. But they were not given enjoyment of it, nor did they benefit from that slumber. Then, as soon as the Caller cried out to them, they rose from the tables of their food while the people were hungry and not satisfied. So how will their condition be at the meeting?

They recognized [the truth] and then denied it, and became blind after they had witnessed the truth and seen it. "That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts, and so they do not comprehend." [al-Munafiqun: 3]

The commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 63, verses 2–3:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 63, verse 4:

They are the most handsome of people in bodies, the most eloquent of tongues, the most refined in speech, the most corrupt in hearts, and the weakest in courage. They are like propped-up pieces of wood that bear no fruit. They have been uprooted from their planting places and lean against a wall that holds them up, so that travelers will not step on them. ﴿When you see them, their bodies impress you; and if they speak, you listen to what they say. They are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4].

They delay the prayer from its first time until the time of "the sunrise of the dead": the Subh prayer until the sun rises, and the 'Asr prayer until sunset. They peck at it like the crow pecks, for it is the prayer of the bodies, not the prayer of the hearts. They look around during it like the fox looks around, for it is certain that it is hunted and pursued. They do not attend the congregation; rather, if one of them prays, he prays in the house or the shop. When he disputes, he deviates from the truth; when he makes a covenant, he betrays it; when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays. This is their dealing with the creation, and that is their dealing with the Creator. So take their description from the beginning of al-Mutaffifin to the end of al-Sama' wal-Tariq, for none informs you of their attributes like one who is well-informed. ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [al-Tahrim: 9]. How numerous they are, though they are the fewest! How cowardly they are, though they are the most abject! How ignorant they are, though they claim to be knowledgeable! How deceived they are regarding Allah, for they are ignorant of His greatness! ﴿They swear by Allah that they are surely of you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are fearful.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 56].

(Faida: a note)

It has been said, regarding His words ﴿When you see them, their bodies impress you; and if they speak, you listen to what they say. They are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾, that the intended person is 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, who was among the most handsome of people in body. The correct view is that the expression is general, applying to whoever has these attributes: soundness and completeness of body, fine speech, and emptiness of the spirit of faith and love of guidance and preference for it. They are like cut pieces of wood that lean on one another, empty of the spirit of life that growth or increase gives, and fruitlessness, and characterized by cowardice and feebleness, such that their possessor thinks every cry is aimed at him.

Therefore, it is an extreme deficiency to say that the intended person in this expression is 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy.

(Section: on the category of the zanadiqa (hidden disbelievers))

They are a people who outwardly show Islam and following the messengers, while inwardly concealing disbelief and enmity toward Allah and His Messenger.

These are the hypocrites, and they are in the lowest level of the Fire. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper.﴾ [al-Nisa': 145].

So the openly disbelieving disbelievers are lighter, and they are above them in the levels of the Fire, because both groups share disbelief and enmity toward Allah and His messengers, but the hypocrites added to them lying and hypocrisy. The affliction of the Muslims by them is greater than their affliction by the open disbelievers. For this reason, Allah the Exalted said about them: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4].

Such an expression implies restriction, meaning: there is no enemy except them. However, the restriction of enmity to them is not what is intended here, nor that they are the only enemies of the Muslims. Rather, this affirms their priority and their greater right to this attribute, and that one should not imagine, because of their outward affiliation with the Muslims, their loyalty to them, and their mixing with them, that they are not their enemies. Rather, they are more deserving of enmity than one who separates from them in dwelling and openly sets enmity against them.

The harm of these who mix with them and associate with them, while inwardly opposed to their religion, is more severe for them than the harm of one who openly declares enmity; it is more constant and more lasting. This is because war with the latter lasts an hour or some days, then it ends and is followed by victory and triumph. But these are with them in homes and dwellings morning and evening, revealing the enemy's weaknesses to him and waiting for misfortunes to befall them, and they cannot be fought openly. So they are more deserving of enmity than the separated, openly declared one. For this reason it was said: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾.

This does not mean that there is no enemy to you except them, but that they are more deserving of being your enemy than the openly disbelieving disbelievers.

A parallel to this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ):

"The poor man is not the wanderer who is turned away by one morsel or two morsels, one date or two dates. Rather, the poor man is the one who does not ask people, and no one notices him so as to give him charity."

This is not a negation of the name "poor" from the wanderer, but an information that this contented one, whom they do not call poor, is more deserving of this name than the wanderer whom they call poor.

The point is that this category is the most wretched of the wretched. For this reason, they will be mocked in the Hereafter. They will be given a light by which they walk through the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), then Allah extinguishes their light and it is said to them: ﴿Return behind you and seek light﴾ [al-Hadid: 13].

A wall will be struck between them and the believers: ﴿with a gate, its inner side having mercy, and its outer side facing torment. They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, waited, doubted, and false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah."﴾

Nothing is more intense in regret and affliction than that the path of salvation and success is opened to a servant, until, when he thinks he is saved and sees the dwellings of the happy, he is cut off from them, and wretchedness is struck upon him. We seek refuge in Allah from His anger and His punishment.

This category was in the lowest level only because of the severity of their disbelief. They mixed with the Muslims and associated with them, and encountered the signs of the message and the evidences of faith that those far away did not encounter. They reached knowledge of its truth that did not reach those who openly declared enmity. So when they disbelieve despite this knowledge, they are more severe in disbelief, more corrupt in hearts, and more hostile to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers than those far away, even if those far away are prepared to fight the Muslims.

For this reason Allah the Exalted said [about the hypocrites]: ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts, so they do not understand﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 3].

And Allah the Exalted said about them: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 18].

And Allah the Exalted said about the disbelievers: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171].

The disbeliever did not reason, while the hypocrite saw and then became blind, knew and then feigned ignorance, acknowledged and then denied, believed and then disbelieved. Whoever is like this is more severe in disbelief, more corrupt in heart, and more rebellious against Allah and His messengers, so he deserves the lowest level.

(Section: Sins cast terror and fear into the hearts)

Among their punishments is the terror and fear that Allah, glorified and exalted, casts into the heart of the disobedient person, so you see him only fearful and terrified.

Indeed, obedience is Allah's greatest fortress. Whoever enters it is among those safe from the punishments of this world and the Hereafter. Whoever leaves it is encompassed by fears from every side. So whoever obeys Allah, the fears are turned into safety for him, and whoever disobeys Him, his places of safety are turned into fears. You find the disobedient person only with a heart as if it were between the wings of a bird: if the wind moves the door, he says, "The pursuit has come!" If he hears the sound of a footstep, he fears it may be a herald of destruction. He thinks every cry is against him and every harm is aimed at him. Whoever fears Allah, He makes him safe from everything, and whoever does not fear Allah, He makes him fear everything:

> Thus Allah decreed among the creation since they were created,
> that fears and crimes are in one yoke.

(Sins cause loneliness)

Among their punishments is that they cause a great loneliness in the heart, so the sinner finds himself estranged. Estrangement has fallen between him and his Lord, between him and the creation, and between him and himself. Whenever sins increase, the estrangement intensifies. The harshest life is the life of the estranged and fearful, and the most pleasant life is the life of those who are at ease. So if the sensible person looked and weighed the pleasure of disobedience against the fear and estrangement it produces, he would know the badness of his state and the magnitude of his loss, for he sold the intimacy, safety, and sweetness of obedience for the loneliness of disobedience and the fear and harm that it necessitates.

As it has been said:

> If sins have made you lonely,
> then leave them, if you wish, and find intimacy.

The secret of the matter is that obedience necessitates nearness to the Lord, glorified is He. Whenever nearness intensifies, intimacy grows strong. Disobedience necessitates distance from the Lord, and whenever distance increases, loneliness grows strong.

For this reason, a servant feels estrangement between himself and his enemy because of the distance between them, even if he is close to him and in contact with him, and he finds strong intimacy between himself and the one he loves, even if he is far from him.

Loneliness is caused by a veil, and whenever the veil thickens, loneliness increases. Heedlessness necessitates loneliness, and more severe than it is the loneliness of disobedience, and more severe than that is the loneliness of polytheism and disbelief. You will not find anyone engaged in any of that except that loneliness overtakes him in proportion to what he has engaged in. So loneliness covers his face and heart, and he becomes estranged and is shunned by others.

(Fāʾidah — a benefit or point of insight)

Allah, glorified is He, has made honour (ʿizz) the companion of obedience to Him, and humiliation (dhull) the companion of disobedience to Him. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾.

And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 139].

Faith (al-īmān) is speech and action, outward and inward. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Whoever desires honour — then to Allah belongs all honour. To Him ascend the good words, and righteous action raises them﴾ [Fāṭir: 10].

That is: whoever desires honour, let him seek it through obedience to Allah and His remembrance, by means of good words and righteous action.

In the supplication of the qunūt (al-qunūt, the supplication in the prayer): "Indeed, the one whom You befriend is never humiliated, and the one whom You oppose is never honoured."

Whoever obeys Allah has befriended Him in what He obeyed Him in, and he has of honour in proportion to his obedience. Whoever disobeys Him has opposed Him in what he disobeyed Him in, and he has of humiliation in proportion to his disobedience.

He said in (Ighāthat al-Lahfān):

One of the early pious predecessors (al-salaf) said: "People seek honour at the doors of kings, and they do not find it except in obedience to Allah."

Al-Ḥasan (al-Baṣrī) said: "Even if mules prance with them and mounts trot with them, the humiliation of sin is indeed in their hearts. Allah, mighty and majestic, refuses except to humiliate whoever disobeys Him. That is because whoever obeys Allah, the Exalted, has befriended Him, and the one whom Allah befriends is not humiliated, as in the supplication of the qunūt."

(Fāʾidah)

The servant has of elevation in proportion to the faith he possesses, and Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 8].

So he has of honour in proportion to the faith he possesses and its realities. Whenever he misses a share of elevation and honour, it is in exchange for what he has missed of the realities of faith, in knowledge and in action, outward and inward.

(Faṣl — section)

Honour (ʿizz) is the opposite of humiliation (dhull), and humiliation's root meaning is weakness and incapacity. Thus honour entails completeness of power and might, and for this reason it is attributed to the believer and is not blameworthy for him, unlike arrogance (kibr).

A man said to al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī: "You are arrogant." He said: "I am not arrogant, but I am honourable (ʿazīz)."

And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 8].

And ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said: "We have not ceased to be honoured since ʿUmar embraced Islam."

And the Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, strengthen Islam by one of these two men: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, or Abū Jahl ibn Hishām."

And in some reports: "Indeed, people seek honour at the doors of kings, and they do not find it except in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic."

And in a hadith: "O Allah, honour us through Your obedience, and do not humiliate us through Your disobedience."

And one of them said: "Whoever wants honour without authority, multitude without clan, and wealth without money, let him move from the humiliation of sin to the honour of obedience."

So honour is of the same kind as power and strength.

And it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, yet there is good in both."

Power, if it is not accompanied by wisdom — but rather the one who has power does whatever he wills without consideration of the outcome, and without a praiseworthy wisdom that he seeks by his will and intends by his act — his act is corruption, like the owner of desires of error and oppression, who uses his strength to achieve what he wants of the desires of error in his belly and his private parts, and of oppressing people. Although such a person has strength and honour, since wisdom is not joined to it, that becomes a help for his evil and corruption.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 63, verse 9:

Ibn Jurayj said: I heard ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah say: it is the obligatory prayer (al-salat al-maktubah).

The argument from the verse is that God pronounced absolute loss upon the one whom his wealth and children distracted from the prayer, and absolute loss only befalls the disbelievers, for the Muslim, even if he suffers loss through his sins and disobedience, his final end is gain. This is clarified by the fact that God, glorified and exalted is He, emphasised the loss of the one who abandons the prayer in this verse by several kinds of emphasis:

The first: His use of the nominal form (lafẓ al-ism), which indicates the establishment and permanence of the loss, rather than the verbal form, which indicates renewal and occurrence.

The second: Prefixing the noun with the definite article (al-alif wa-l-lam), which conveys the attainment of the complete state of the one named. For when you say, "Zayd is the knowledgeable, righteous one," this establishes the perfection of that quality for him, unlike your saying "a knowledgeable, righteous one."

The third: His placing the subject and predicate both in the definite form, and this is among the signs of the predicate being restricted to the subject, as in His saying, ﴿And those are the successful (al-mufliḥūn)﴾, and His saying, ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers (al-ẓālimūn)﴾, ﴿Those are the true believers (al-mu'minūna ḥaqqan)﴾, and its like.

The fourth: The insertion of the separating pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl) between the subject and the predicate, which, along with separation, conveys two further benefits: the strengthening of the predication, and the restriction of the predicated subject to the predicate, as in His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy (al-Ghaniyy al-Ḥamīd)﴾, His saying, ﴿And Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, and His saying, ﴿Indeed, He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾.

And the like of these.

(Section)

The point: since continual remembrance (dawam al-dhikr) is the cause of continual love, and Allah, glorified is He, is most worthy of complete love, worship, glorification and reverence, then abundant remembrance of Him is among the most beneficial things for the servant. And his enemy, in truth, is the one who turns him away from the remembrance of his Lord and from His worship.

For this reason, He, glorified is He, commanded abundant remembrance of Him in the Qur'an, and made it a cause of success. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Remember Allah much, that you may succeed﴾

And He said: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾

And He said: ﴿And the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember﴾

And He said: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that — then those are the losers﴾

And He said: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾

And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The mufarridūn have gone ahead." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the mufarridūn?" He said: "Those who remember Allah much."

In al-Tirmidhi, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than spending gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike yours?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The remembrance of Allah."

It is also in the Muwatta' as a statement of Abu al-Darda' (mawquf).

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "No son of Adam has done a deed that is more effective in saving him from the punishment of Allah than the remembrance of Allah."

Mentioning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) follows from his remembrance.

The point: continual remembrance is a cause of continual love.

So remembrance for the heart is like water for the crop, rather like water for the fish; it has no life except by it.

It has kinds: remembrance of Him by His names and attributes, and praising Him by them.

The second: glorifying Him, praising Him, magnifying Him, proclaiming His oneness (tahlil) and exalting Him, and this is the predominant use of the term dhikr among the later scholars.

The third: remembrance of Him through His rulings, commands and prohibitions. This is the remembrance of the people of knowledge; indeed, the three kinds together are their remembrance of their Lord.

Among the best of His remembrance is remembrance through His speech. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾

Here, His remembrance is His speech which He sent down upon His Messenger. And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah are hearts assured﴾.

And among His remembrance: supplication to Him, seeking His forgiveness, and humbling oneself before Him.

These are five kinds of remembrance.

(Section)

Abundant remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a protection from hypocrisy, for the hypocrites remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but little. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And they do not remember Allah except a little﴾

Ka'b said: Whoever remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, abundantly is cleared of hypocrisy. For this reason, and Allah knows best, Allah, Exalted is He, concluded Surah al-Munafiqun with His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that — then those are the losers.﴾

Indeed, in that is a warning against the trial of the hypocrites, who neglected the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and so fell into hypocrisy.

Some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were asked about the Kharijites: "Are they hypocrites?"

He said: "No. The hypocrites do not remember Allah except a little."

So the scarcity of the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is among the signs of hypocrisy, and abundant remembrance of Him is a protection from hypocrisy. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is too generous to afflict a heart that remembers Him with hypocrisy; rather that afflicts only hearts that have become heedless of the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

(Section: On explaining the benefit of the Truth and the benefit of creation, and the difference between them)

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after some discussion:

Once this is clarified, it becomes apparent that none of the created beings seeks your benefit as a primary aim; rather he seeks his own benefit through you. And there may be harm to you in that if the lover does not observe justice. So if you call upon him, you have called upon one whose harm is nearer than his benefit.

As for the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, He wants you for your own sake and for your benefit, not so that He may benefit from you. That is pure benefit for you with no harm in it. So reflect on this with the fullest reflection and observe it with the fullest observance. Let this insight restrain you from hoping in the created or seeking benefit for yourself from them, for he does not desire that in the primary intent at all; rather he desires his own benefit from you, sooner or later. He wants himself, not you; and he wants the benefit of himself through you, not your benefit through himself. So contemplate this, for in it is great benefit, ease, and despair of created beings, closing the door of your servitude to them and opening the door of servitude to Allah alone. How great is the portion of one who knows this matter and observes it with the fullest observance.

This should not drive you to harshness toward people, to abandoning kindness to them, or to bearing their harm with patience; rather be kind to them for Allah's sake, not for their sake.

Just as you should not fear them, you should not hope in them. Among what clarifies this is that most people seek to attain their need through you, even if that is harmful to you. For the one in need is blind, seeing nothing but the fulfilment of his need. They do not care about your harm once they attain their need from you; indeed, even if it meant the ruin of your worldly life and your Hereafter, they would not care.

When the intelligent person reflects on this, he knows that it is enmity in the form of friendship, and that for the discerning person there is no greater enemy than this enmity. They want to make you like a bellows that inflates your belly and squeezes your ribs for their benefit and interests. Indeed, if they were permitted to eat you, they would slaughter you as they slaughter a sheep. How often do they slaughter you at every moment without a knife, for their interests! How often have they taken you as a bridge and a passage to their aims while you are unaware! How often have they sold your Hereafter for their worldly life while you do not know, and perhaps you do know!

How often have they sold your portion from Allah for their portions from you, and you return empty-handed! How often have they made you miss the benefits of both abodes, cut you off from them, and blocked your way between you and them, cutting the road of your journey to your first abodes and the home to which you were called; and they say: "We are your beloved and your servants, your supporters and your helpers, those who strive for your interests." And they lie, by Allah! They are enemies in the form of friends, a war in the form of peacemakers, and highwaymen in the form of helpers.

So, O for my succour! Then O for my succour, by Allah who gives succour and is not given succour! ﴿O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ [al-Taghabun: 14]

﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that — then those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

The fortunate, successful one is he who deals with them for Allah's sake and does not deal with Allah for their sake; who fears Allah regarding them and does not fear them regarding Allah; who pleases Allah at the cost of their displeasure and does not please them at the cost of Allah's displeasure; who keeps watch for Allah regarding them and does not keep watch over them regarding Allah; who prefers Allah over them and does not prefer them regarding Allah; who extinguishes from his heart his fear, hope and love for them, and revives in it love of Allah, fear of Him and hope in Him. This is the one who is written down against them, and whose dealings with them are all gain, on condition that he bears their harm patiently, takes it as spoils and not as a burden, and as profit and not as loss.

What further clarifies the matter is that none of the created beings can ever repel from you any harm except by the permission of Allah, His will, His decree and His measure. So He is in reality the One who alone brings good deeds, and alone removes evil deeds: ﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, there is no repeller of His bounty﴾ [Yunus: 107]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas:

"Know that if the creation gathered together to benefit you, they would not benefit you except with something Allah had written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you, they would not harm you except with something Allah had written against you."

And if this is the condition of the created, then attaching fear and hope to them is harmful, not beneficial. And Allah knows best.
